newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-LONARD WINS AUSTRALIAN MASTERS AS WOODS FALTERS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LONARD WINS AUSTRALIAN MASTERS AS WOODS FALTERS.

text.p: Peter Lonard scored his first professional victory on Sunday when he won the Australian Masters after the expected challenge from Tiger Woods failed to materialise.
Lonard beat fellow Australian Peter O'Malley on the second hole of a playoff after the pair were tied on 276, 16 under par.
Woods, the overwhelming favourite for the title, made no impression on the leaders with a level-par 73.
He finished joint eighth on nine under with fellow American Larry Mize and Australian veteran Rodger Davis.
Lonard, whose career was badly interrupted when he succumbed to a rare tropical disease five years ago, proved a model of consistency, firing a 69 in each round.
"This is probably the greatest day of the my life," 29-year-old Lonard said.
In his previous 11 tournaments, the 1990 Australasian Tour Rookie of the Year finished in the top 10 on seven occasions, including three consecutive second places.
O'Malley, the overnight leader by one shot, fired three successive birdies on the back nine in his round of 72 to join Lonard in a playoff.
